findings.defect: The Korean internet shorthand signals agreement before the upvote; retaining the unexplained digits omits that pragmatic meaning.
findings.rationale: Both the commenter’s agreement and their recommendation should be conveyed.

findings.current: └ “Filling his own pockets,” lol. The thing built up in your parents’ bodies is the *sari*; what’s coming out of my mouth is profanity.
findings.defect: The translation replaces 사리사욕 with an unrelated phrase, leaving the subsequent 사리 wordplay unexplained and incoherent in English.
findings.rationale: The source twists part of the preceding accusation 사리사욕 into a bodily-deposit insult, then contrasts it with 쌍욕, or vicious profanity.
findings.replacement: └ “Self-interest,” lol. The only interest here is the deposits building up in your parents’ bodies; what’s coming out of my mouth is pure profanity.
findings.source: └ 윗 댓글 사리사욕ㅋㅋㅋ 너희 부모님 몸에 쌓인 게 사리고, 내 입에서 나오는 건 쌍욕임.

findings.current: Even as people were banned from wearing dentures, using hearing aids, and entering the senior center in droves, the fighting didn’t stop.
findings.defect: The draft changes the running joke from the commenters having their dentures and hearing aids confiscated to being forbidden from wearing or using them.
findings.rationale: The narration literalizes the preceding escalating “confiscated” replies and must retain that mechanism.
findings.replacement: Even as people everywhere had their dentures and hearing aids confiscated and were banned from the senior center, the fighting didn’t stop.
findings.source: 곳곳에서 틀니와 보청기, 노인정 출입을 금지당한 사람들이 속출했음에도 싸움은 멈추지 않았다.

findings.current:
Hyeongseok, go drink more milk from your mommy and study some more~~`!!

└ You drink more.
findings.defect: Rendering 젖을 먹다 as merely drinking milk sanitizes the infantilizing command to go nurse from his mother and weakens the comeback built on the same verb.
findings.rationale: The source uses nursing as an insult and immediately repeats the action in Hyeongseok’s retort.
findings.replacement:
Young Hyeongseok, go back to your mommy, suck some more milk, and study harder~~`!!

└ You go suck some more.
findings.source:
형석군은 엄마한테 가서 젖을 더먹고 공부 더하고 오너라~~`!!

└ 니나 더 먹어.

findings.defect: The draft substantially sanitizes the compound profanity and removes the lowborn/commoner insult.
findings.rationale: 호로 쌍놈의 새끼 is markedly stronger and more socially loaded than “rotten bastard.”
findings.replacement: └ You’re a goddamn lowborn son of a bitch.

findings.defect: The draft expands the acronym before the next commenter asks what it means, destroying the setup-and-reveal structure of the joke.
findings.rationale: 제꼬삼 is an opaque abbreviation whose full crude meaning is deliberately revealed only in the following exchange.

findings.current: The strength to stop two major catastrophes, the second time by himself, and to defeat a Named Monster alone.
findings.defect: The draft invents that Taekyung stopped the second catastrophe by himself. The source applies 홀로 only to defeating the Named Monster.
findings.rationale: The modifier 홀로 directly governs 네임드 몬스터를 쓰러트린, not either of the two catastrophes.
findings.replacement: He had already prevented two major catastrophes and possessed the strength to defeat a Named Monster all by himself.
findings.source: 대참사를 이미 두 번이나 막은 데다 홀로 네임드 몬스터를 쓰러트린 힘.

findings.current:
“Because it’s a waste.”

—Pardon?

“It’s a waste, but it’s necessary, isn’t it? Please continue.”
findings.defect: Calling the donation “a waste” implies that it is a bad use of the money, whereas 아깝다 means he hates parting with money that he still recognizes must be spent.
findings.rationale: Taekyung is lamenting the personal loss while affirming the donation’s necessity, not condemning the donation as wasteful.
findings.replacement:
“Because I hate parting with the money.”

—Pardon?

“I hate giving it up, but this is necessary. Please continue.”
findings.source:
“아까워서요.”

- 예?

“아깝지만 필요한 일이잖아요. 계속 진행해 주세요.”

findings.current:
This wasn’t a matter of hundreds or thousands. It was hundreds of billions.

It was a truly staggering sum, and I nearly made a sound to match.
findings.defect: The draft incorrectly changes the named numerical unit 억 into “hundreds of billions” and erases the repeated 억 wordplay connecting the unit to an exclamation of shock.
findings.rationale: The source emphasizes that the account is counted in units of one hundred million won, then makes a pun on the identical exclamation 억.
findings.replacement:
The unit wasn’t hundreds or thousands. It was *eok*—hundreds of millions.[^2]

It was literally an *eok*-inducing sum, and I nearly cried out myself.

[^2]: *Eok* is both the Korean unit for one hundred million and an exclamation of shock.
findings.source:
단위가 백도, 천도 아니다. 억이다, 억.

그야말로 억 소리 나는 금액이었고, 실제로 그런 소리가 나올 뻔했다.

findings.current: The surroundings had long since fallen into darkness, while the inside of the brightly lit pavilion was warm and clear.
findings.defect: The draft invents warmth and renders 환했다 as “clear” rather than describing the pavilion’s brightness.
findings.rationale: The sentence contrasts the darkness outside with the bright interior; it says nothing about temperature.
findings.replacement: Darkness had long since swallowed the surroundings, while the illuminated pavilion shone brightly.
findings.source: 사방은 어둠에 잠긴 지 오래였고 불 밝힌 전각 안은 환했다.

summary: The draft contains one critical alteration of who acted alone, along with several meaningful losses in joke mechanics, profanity, quantity explanation, and scene detail.
